record.statement: Prove that the three-dimensional Ising model is non-trivial: its scaling limit is not a Gaussian field (the renormalised coupling constant does not vanish).
record.status_search: The second half of the source's Conjecture 6 (triviality in d = 4) was proved by Aizenman and Duminil-Copin, 'Marginal triviality of the scaling limits of critical 4D Ising and phi^4 models', Ann. of Math. 194 (2021) 163-235 (arXiv 1912.07973); the d = 3 non-triviality half remains open per the bounded search of 2026-09-07.
record.title: Non-triviality of the scaling limit of the three-dimensional Ising model

record.author: claude-probability-1000-continue-0907
record.key_identity: Non-triviality <=> inf_L P(two independent currents at scale L intersect) > 0; second moment reduces this to a two-point lower bound (C0051) plus a variance estimate.
record.method: Use the random-current representation: non-triviality is equivalent to non-vanishing of the intersection probability of two random currents at large scales.
record.obstruction: Variance of the intersection count needs six-point correlations beyond Lebowitz.
record.result: By Aizenman's identity the four-point Ursell function U_4(x_1,...,x_4) is expressed through the probability that the currents from x_1 to x_2 and from x_3 to x_4 share a cluster; non-triviality means the renormalised coupling g = -U_4 summed appropriately does not vanish in the scaling limit, i.e. two independent random-current clusters at scale L intersect with probability bounded below. In d = 3 the clusters have a fractal dimension d_c and two independent such sets in a box of side L intersect with probability of order L^{2 d_c - 3} if they were independent random fractals, which is bounded below iff d_c >= 3/2. The random-current cluster dimension in d = 3 is related to the two-point exponent by d_c = (d + 2 - eta)/2 = (5 - eta)/2 = 2.48 > 3/2, so the heuristic strongly favours non-triviality, and the rigorous gap is that the currents are not independent fractals and the lower bound on the intersection probability must be proved from the model. A rigorous partial statement: if the two-point function satisfies the lower bound of C0051 with exponent 2 - eps, then a second-moment argument on the number of intersection points gives a positive lower bound on the intersection probability at scale L PROVIDED the four-point function is bounded by the product of two-point functions (Lebowitz inequality gives the upper bound in the right direction), so non-triviality would follow from C0051's lower bound plus a variance bound on the intersection count. I did not close the variance bound.

record.title: Duminil-Copin: Lectures on the Ising and Potts models on the hypercubic lattice, PIMS 2017
